tamsin.meet: tamsin|Twelve people have asked me for this plot.
tamsin|You are the first who looked at the ground before the view.
tamsin|Take the book. It has been blank for forty years.
tamsin|I only ever looked at things to price them.
tamsin|Mosslings keep the rocks by the pond. Sit near one and write down what you see.
tamsin|Two columns. What it needs, and what it gives. Fill both.
tamsin|And an axe. You will want a roof before you want anything else.
tamsin|That is the advice. It weighs more than the axe.
tamsin.end: tamsin|(looking west) Evening came early again. A little sooner every week.
tamsin.axe: tamsin|No axe. I will not ask where it went.
tamsin|(taking another from her belt) This one has a notch. So you will know it.
tamsin.tell: tamsin|Shade and mossy stone. And it pays in moss, where the ground is damp.
tamsin|Forty years I walked past them. I never asked what they wanted.
tamsin|Most things out here have two columns. The book has room.
tamsin|Now. The sun is moving. Cut wood, raise a roof, make a bed. Sleep under it.
tamsin|There is a dead garden off the path. Something still tends it. Go gently, tomorrow.
tamsin|I keep the lodge in Hollowmere. Follow the path when you have slept.
tamsin.show: tamsin|(looking down) So that is what kept the old garden.
tamsin|You fed it first. I would have set a snare and priced the tail.
tamsin|Take it to Wren at the kennel. She talks to animals first. Do not take offence.
tamsin|Then the granary. The queen is short of wheat and shorter of sleep.
tamsin.show.alone: tamsin|You have the look of someone followed. Where is it?
tamsin|Fetch it. I would like to see what chose you.
tamsin.festival: tamsin|Odo has a lamp for you. He will introduce you to a loaf first. Bear it.
tamsin|(nodding at the water) Lamps go on the river. Not in the pocket.
tamsin.tonight: tamsin|Festival tonight. I am told to wear the good coat. I own one coat.
tamsin|Be on the bank at dusk.
tamsin.rain: tamsin|(palm out) Forty years underground. I never once got rained on. Stand in it.
tamsin.pet: tamsin|(to the leaftail) Still following? Good judge.
tamsin|Has it brought you a seed yet? It will. Nobody asked it to.
tamsin.bed: tamsin|You slept under your own roof. It shows. You stand differently.
tamsin.watch.half: tamsin|Shade and mossy stone. Good. That is what it needs.
tamsin|Now what it gives. Watch the ones on damp ground, by the pond. Be patient.
tamsin.watch: tamsin|The rocks, in the shade. Sit still. They will not perform for you.
tamsin|(heeling a seedling into a boot print) Go on. The book is waiting.
tamsin.roof.wood: tamsin|Oak takes an axe well. Twelve logs will do.
tamsin|(pressing an acorn into the turf) Do not mind me. Old habit.
tamsin.roof.build: tamsin|A bed wants planks and fiber. Fiber comes off leaves, if you keep at them.
tamsin|And a block over the bed. Rain does not care how tired you are.
tamsin.roof.sleep: tamsin|Roof is on. Then stop working. The dark is for sleeping.
tamsin.leaftail: tamsin|The garden's keeper startles. Walk as if the floor were asleep.
tamsin|Put the berry down. Then do nothing. Do it well.
tamsin.bread.early: tamsin|The queen is at the granary. Wake her gently. She has earned the nap.
tamsin.bread.grow: tamsin|Wheat wants wet soil and patience. Only one of those comes in a can.
tamsin.bread.deliver: tamsin|Twenty. Take them to her before she counts the sacks a third time.
tamsin.after: tamsin|Still here. Good. The plot will want you in the morning.
tamsin|That lamp is no use in a pocket.
tamsin.fallback: tamsin|(pressing a seedling into a boot print) Mind where you dig. I only fill it in.
maren.deliver: maren|Eighteen. Nineteen. Twenty. You brought twenty.
maren|Forty sacks and twenty sheaves. That is one more week of bread. I will take a week.
maren|Odo gets the first of it tonight. Come to the square at dusk.
maren|That is the good meal. The thanks is this. Thank you.
maren|Then do them fast. Dusk does not wait. I have checked.
maren.deliver.short: maren|(counting your sheaves) That is not twenty. Counting is the one thing I can do.
maren|Come back with twenty. Gus will spot you seed if you are short.
maren.ask: maren|(waking) Forty sacks. I counted twice. It is not enough, and counting again will not make it enough.
maren|Twenty sheaves by the festival. I can pay you in thanks and one good meal.
maren|You are the one on Tamsin's grant. You have a field. I have a winter.
maren|Gus has seed. Tell him I said please. He likes that.
maren|Same fields, same hands, thinner sacks. Gus says the soil is tired.
maren|So am I. Go and see him. He has seed.
maren|They crowned me at sixteen because I could add. Nobody said the adding never stops.
maren|Gus has seed. Go, before I count something.
maren.tonight: maren|Dusk yet? No. Then I can sleep, or you can wait with me.
maren|Then go quietly. I was nearly asleep.
maren.festival: maren|(holding a heel of bread) I am not counting tonight. Ask me tomorrow how many I ate.
maren|Twenty sheaves. I wrote your name in the ledger. In ink.
maren.pet: maren|(one eye open) It has a leaf for a tail. Wren feeds it? Good. One less to count.
maren.waiting: maren|(not looking up) Thirty-nine sacks. A mouse got one. Do not tell Odo.
maren|Rain on the roof. Good. Gus will be unbearable. Good.
maren|Is it grown? No. Then I am still counting.
maren.first: maren|(not opening her eyes) If it is about the sacks, there are forty. Come back later.
maren.after: maren|Your twenty are milled. I counted them once. Once was enough, for once.
gus.more: gus|Came up short. Happens. Soil forgives it.
gus|Four more. Wet them this time. Or don't, and see me again.
gus.seeds.first: gus|Soil's tired. Not lazy. Tired. You'd be too.
gus|Maren sent you. She said please? Huh. She's worried, then.
gus|Hoe. Can. Twelve seeds. Break the ground, plant, keep it wet.
gus|Wet soil grows. Dry soil waits. That's all I know. It's enough.
gus|Rain'd do it better. Rain always does it better.
gus.first: gus|Soil's tired. Not lazy. Tired. You'd be too.
gus|You want seed, see the queen. She keeps the count. I keep the dirt.
gus.seeds: gus|Hoe. Can. Twelve seeds. Break the ground, plant, keep it wet.
gus|Wet soil grows. Dry soil waits. That's all I know. It's enough.
gus|Rain'd do it better. Rain always does it better.
gus|You again. Maren sent you. She said please? Huh.
gus.festival: gus|Good wheat. Short straw, heavy head. Your soil's not tired yet.
gus|Clear night. I'd have liked rain. Don't tell the lamp people.
gus.rain: gus|(hat off, face up) There. Rain.
gus|Go look at your field. It's doing your job for you.
gus.pet: gus|That leaftail digs. Good. Digging's half of farming. Other half's waiting.
gus.grow: gus|Don't watch it. It knows how. Keep it wet and go do something else.
gus|Sleep on it, if it's wet. Wheat does its best work when you're not looking.
gus.deliver: gus|That's twenty. Don't stand here with it. The queen's the one counting.
gus.tonight: gus|Festival tonight. I'll stand at the back. Somebody has to watch the sky.
gus.fallback: gus|It's the soil. Whatever it is. It's the soil.
juniper.first: juniper|You're the new one! From the stone! Have you got any sweets?
juniper|A berry's a sweet. A berry counts. I've got secrets. Good ones.
juniper.festival: juniper|I get to push the stuck lamps off with a stick! Only the stuck ones. That's the rule.
juniper.pet: juniper|It's got a LEAF for a TAIL. Does it know? Don't tell it.
juniper.rain: juniper|I'm not wet, I'm fast. Rain can't land on fast.
juniper.trade: juniper|Is that a berry? That's a sweet! Swap you. One berry, one secret.
juniper|Secret. The queen sleeps on the ledger. It prints numbers on her face. Backwards.
juniper|Secret. Wet wheat grows two whole sizes while you sleep. Gus told the wheat, not me.
juniper|Secret. Odo cried when Gertrude sold. He said onions. There weren't onions.
juniper|Secret. Tamsin's sword is under the lodge floor. She grew beans on top.
juniper|Then no secret. That's the rule. I made it.
juniper.out: juniper|I'm out of secrets. I have to go and find out more. Don't follow me.
juniper.tonight: juniper|Festival's tonight! Odo makes the little sweet ones. I know where he hides them.
juniper.fallback: juniper|No sweets, no secrets. I don't make the rules. I do. I do make them.
